d.chapter: Economic Geography — Sectors of the Economy
d.notions: Tertiary sector, services, trade, transport, communication, banking, tourism, administration.
d.focus: Definition and examples of the tertiary sector, with examples from Cameroon.
d.competence: Learners are able to identify the services they use every day and explain why services are necessary for other sectors.
objectives: Give examples of tertiary activities in Cameroon and explain their importance.
recall: The secondary sector transforms raw materials into finished goods.
It includes agro-industries, heavy industries, construction, energy and crafts.
d.recallNote: Check the homework: four services used by the family every week.
situation: CICAM in Garoua has produced a lot of cloth, but the road to Ngaoundéré is damaged and trucks cannot pass. The cloth stays in the factory, and traders in the South wait for it.
The factory manager says that without transport and traders, the factory cannot sell its goods.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that the cloth cannot reach the traders because the road is damaged and trucks cannot pass.
Who is waiting for the cloth?
Traders in the South of the country are waiting for the cloth.
What can be done to solve this problem?
The road can be repaired, or the cloth can be sent by another route, such as the railway from Ngaoundéré.
d.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the tertiary sector, whose services link producers to consumers.

qa.q: Transporters, traders, teachers and doctors do not produce goods. What do they provide, and what sector do they belong to?
qa.a: They provide services. They belong to the tertiary sector.

sum.title: I. Definition
defs: The tertiary sector is the sector of the economy that provides services to people and businesses.

qa.q: Name three means of transport used in Cameroon.
qa.a: Road transport (buses, trucks, moto-taxis), rail transport (Camrail, from Douala to Ngaoundéré), air transport (Garoua airport) and sea transport (port of Douala).

qa.q: Name two social services provided by the state.
qa.a: Education in schools and health care in hospitals are social services.

qa.q: Mobile money, banks and telephone companies are also services. How do they help people?
qa.a: They help people to save, send and receive money and to communicate quickly.

qa.q: Why do tourists visit North Cameroon? Which sector does tourism belong to?
qa.a: Tourists visit the national parks of Benoue, Bouba Ndjida and Waza, and the Rhumsiki landscapes. Tourism belongs to the tertiary sector.

sum.title: II. Examples of Tertiary Activities
sum.intro: The main tertiary activities, with examples from Cameroon, are the following:
items: A. Trade
Trade is the buying and selling of goods in markets, shops and supermarkets, and between countries.
B. Transport and Communication
Transport moves people and goods by road, rail, air and sea. Communication includes telephone, internet, post and media.
C. Banking and Insurance
Banks, microfinance and mobile money help people to save, borrow and send money.
D. Social Services and Administration
Education, health care, security and public administration are provided mostly by the state.
E. Tourism
Tourists visit national parks such as Waza and Benoue, beaches such as Kribi and Limbe, and cultural sites.

evaluation: The tertiary sector is the sector that provides services to people and businesses.
Three tertiary activities are trade, transport and banking.
Why does the secondary sector need the tertiary sector?
Factories need transport and traders to deliver and sell their goods.
remediation: The sector that provides services is the ______ sector.
The buying and selling of goods is called ______.
The railway company of Cameroon is ______.
The main seaport of Cameroon is ______.
Visiting national parks for pleasure is called ______.
d.remediationAnswers: 1. tertiary 2. trade 3. Camrail 4. Douala 5. social 6. tourism
